Select the OBD from Completed U-BOIN Trials

Source: R/uboin_select_obd.R
uboin_select_obd.Rd

Choose the optimal biological dose (OBD) of the U-BOIN design for each of a set of completed trials from the numbers of patients with each outcome at each dose.

Usage

uboin_select_obd(
  n_outcome,
  tox_upper,
  resp_lower,
  eliminated = NULL,
  utility = c(0, 30, 50, 100),
  cutoff_eli = 0.95,
  cutoff_eli_resp = 0.9,
  prior_tox = c(1, 1),
  prior_resp = c(1, 1)
)

Arguments

n_outcome

Integer matrix with one row per dose and four columns, the numbers of patients with the outcomes (no response, DLT), (no response, no DLT), (response, DLT) and (response, no DLT) in one trial, or an integer array with dimensions trial by dose by outcome for several trials, as returned by uboin_simulate.

tox_upper

Numeric scalar. Highest acceptable DLT probability.

resp_lower

Numeric scalar. Lowest acceptable response probability.

eliminated

Logical vector with one element per dose for one trial, a logical matrix with one row per trial for several, or NULL. Doses eliminated in stage I, which cannot be selected. Defaults to NULL, none.

utility

Numeric vector of length four. Utility of the four outcomes, in the order of the columns of n_outcome. Defaults to c(0, 30, 50, 100).

cutoff_eli

Numeric scalar. Cutoff of the toxicity rule. Defaults to 0.95.

cutoff_eli_resp

Numeric scalar. Cutoff of the futility rule. Defaults to 0.90.

prior_tox

Numeric vector of length two. Beta prior of the toxicity rule. Defaults to c(1, 1).

prior_resp

Numeric vector of length two. Beta prior of the futility rule. Defaults to c(1, 1).

Value

A data frame with one row per trial and columns

trial

Trial index.

obd

Selected dose level, or NA when no dose is admissible.

reason

"selected" or "no_admissible_dose".

utility_DL1, ...

Posterior mean utility of each dose.

admissible_DL1, ...

Whether each dose is admissible: tried, not eliminated, neither toxic nor futile.

Details

The OBD is the admissible dose with the largest posterior mean utility, the lowest among ties, with the rules of rule B2 described in uboin_simulate.

References

Zhou, Y., Lee, J. J. and Yuan, Y. (2019). A utility-based Bayesian optimal interval (U-BOIN) phase I/II design to identify the optimal biological dose for targeted and immune therapies. Statistics in Medicine, 38(28), S5299-S5316. doi:10.1002/sim.8361

See also

uboin_simulate, sim_uboin

Examples

# Table S3 of the supporting information of the article, with its utilities
n_outcome <- rbind(c(0, 3, 0, 0),
                   c(0, 2, 0, 1),
                   c(0, 3, 1, 1),
                   c(1, 3, 1, 4),
                   c(1, 2, 1, 2))
uboin_select_obd(n_outcome, tox_upper = 0.30, resp_lower = 0.20,
                 utility = c(0, 15, 25, 100))
#>   trial obd   reason utility_DL1 utility_DL2 utility_DL3 utility_DL4
#> 1     1   4 selected          20       41.25    34.16667        50.5
#>   utility_DL5 admissible_DL1 admissible_DL2 admissible_DL3 admissible_DL4
#> 1    41.42857           TRUE           TRUE           TRUE           TRUE
#>   admissible_DL5
#> 1           TRUE
